original_question: For a fixed prime p, does there exist a polynomial M_p(T) in Q[T] such that mu(g, p) >= M_p(g) for every genus g >= 2, and equality mu(g, p) = M_p(g) holds for infinitely many genera? Here mu(g, p) is the maximum number of automorphisms of a smooth projective genus-g curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p.
target_in_paper: Section 9, Question 9.3, "Minimal maximal number of automorphisms of curves".
correct_elements: Your draft captures the paper's actual target very closely: it fixes a prime p, asks for a polynomial M_p in Q[T], requires the inequality mu(g,p) >= M_p(g) for every genus g >= 2, and asks that equality hold for infinitely many genera. Your definition of mu(g,p) as the maximal size of the automorphism group of a genus-g curve in characteristic p is also faithful in substance.
missing_details: The paper quantifies over curves over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, not just abstractly over characteristic p.

The paper defines mu(g,p) as the maximum of #Aut(C) over all complete, irreducible, nonsingular algebraic curves C of genus g defined over k; your "smooth projective" formulation is equivalent, but the paper states it in that older language.
The paper explicitly states that once the characteristic is fixed, mu(g,p) does not depend on the choice of algebraically closed field k.
The genus variable is quantified as an integer g in Z_{>=2}.

The exact target is posed as Question 9.3, immediately after Theorem 9.2, which settles the characteristic-zero analogue; so the question should remain restricted to prime p and not be broadened to include p=0.
refined_question: Fix a prime number p. Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, and for each integer g >= 2 let mu(g,p) denote the maximum of #Aut(C) as C ranges over all complete, irreducible, nonsingular algebraic curves of genus g defined over k (equivalently, smooth projective genus-g curves over k). Does there exist a polynomial M_p(T) in Q[T] such that mu(g,p) >= M_p(g) for every integer g >= 2, and such that mu(g,p) = M_p(g) for infinitely many values of g?
justification: The draft is aiming at the short open problem in Section 9 on the function mu(g,p). Definition 9.1 introduces mu(g,char(k)) and states its independence of the chosen algebraically closed field of that characteristic. Theorem 9.2 records the characteristic-zero case, including the lower bound mu(g,0) >= 8(g+1) and equality for infinitely many g. Question 9.3 then asks for the prime-characteristic analogue exactly in the form of existence of a polynomial M_p in Q[T] with a universal lower-bound property and equality for infinitely many genera. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is essentially your draft plus the ambient field, the exact class of curves, and the integer quantifiers.
